answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a shared-infrastructure audit: identities that share a device fingerprint, payment trail, or network origin are grouped into one cluster, and that cluster's total reward is capped no matter how many accounts it holds. Like a gale scattering ships that try to sail under one flag, the audit splits one prize across the cluster instead of multiplying it. An honest island of one agent keeps its full reward, while a farmer's thousand fakes on the same horizon of infrastructure earn no more together than a single account, so cloning costs work but buys nothing.
